presets.label: pgr_dijkstra — one to one
sql: -- Shortest path from vertex 5 to vertex 12 on the directed sample graph.
SELECT * FROM pgr_dijkstra('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 5, 12);

presets.label: pgr_dijkstra — many to many, undirected
sql: -- Every start in the first list to every end in the second, ignoring edge direction.
SELECT * FROM pgr_dijkstra('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', [5, 3], [12, 17], directed => false);

presets.label: pgr_dijkstra — pairs from a table
sql: -- Only the (source, target) pairs listed in the combinations table.
SELECT * FROM pgr_dijkstra('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT source, target FROM combinations');

presets.label: pgr_dijkstraCost
sql: -- Just the total cost of each route, without the path.
SELECT * FROM pgr_dijkstraCost('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', [5, 3], [12, 17]);

presets.label: pgr_dijkstraCostMatrix
sql: -- Costs between every ordered pair of the listed vertices.
SELECT * FROM pgr_dijkstraCostMatrix('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', [5, 7, 12, 16]);

presets.label: pgr_dijkstraNear
sql: -- The route from vertex 5 to whichever of 12, 15 and 17 is cheapest to reach.
SELECT * FROM pgr_dijkstraNear('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 5, [12, 15, 17]);

presets.label: pgr_dijkstraNearCost
sql: -- The same nearest target, cost only.
SELECT * FROM pgr_dijkstraNearCost('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 5, [12, 15, 17]);

presets.label: pgr_dijkstraVia
sql: -- One route through 5, 7, 1, 8 and 15 in that order; path_id numbers the legs,
-- route_agg_cost runs along the whole route.
SELECT * FROM pgr_dijkstraVia('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', [5, 7, 1, 8, 15]);

presets.label: pgr_withPoints
sql: -- From point of interest 1 to point 3; negative ids are points, details shows points passed.
SELECT * FROM pgr_withPoints('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT pid, edge_id, fraction, side FROM pointsofinterest', -1, -3, details => true);

presets.label: pgr_withPointsCost
sql: -- Costs between points and vertices mixed together.
SELECT * FROM pgr_withPointsCost('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT pid, edge_id, fraction, side FROM pointsofinterest', [-1, 5], [-3, 12]);

presets.label: pgr_withPointsCostMatrix
sql: -- A cost matrix over two points and one vertex.
SELECT * FROM pgr_withPointsCostMatrix('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT pid, edge_id, fraction, side FROM pointsofinterest', [-1, -3, 5]);

presets.label: pgr_withPointsVia
sql: -- A route through point 1, vertex 7, point 3, vertex 16 and vertex 15, in that order.
SELECT * FROM pgr_withPointsVia('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT pid, edge_id, fraction, side FROM pointsofinterest', [-1, 7, -3, 16, 15]);

presets.label: pgr_withPointsDD
sql: -- Everything within a cost of 2 from points 1 and 5, one colour per start; 'r' drives on the right.
SELECT * FROM pgr_withPointsDD('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT pid, edge_id, fraction, side FROM pointsofinterest', [-1, -5], 2.0, 'r');

presets.label: pgr_withPointsKSP
sql: -- The three cheapest routes from point 1 to point 2, one colour per path_id.
SELECT * FROM pgr_withPointsKSP('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT pid, edge_id, fraction, side FROM pointsofinterest', -1, -2, 3, 'r');

presets.label: pgr_bdDijkstra
sql: -- Bidirectional search: from both ends at once.
SELECT * FROM pgr_bdDijkstra('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 5, 12);

presets.label: pgr_bdDijkstraCost
sql: -- Bidirectional search, cost only.
SELECT * FROM pgr_bdDijkstraCost('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', [5, 3], [12, 17]);

presets.label: pgr_bdDijkstraCostMatrix
sql: -- Bidirectional search over every ordered pair.
SELECT * FROM pgr_bdDijkstraCostMatrix('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', [5, 7, 12, 16]);

presets.label: pgr_aStar
sql: -- A* from 5 to 12, steered by the straight-line distance to the goal; compare pgr_dijkstra.
-- The edges carry their end-point coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2).
SELECT * FROM pgr_aStar('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost, x1, y1, x2, y2 FROM edges', 5, 12);

presets.label: pgr_aStarCost
sql: -- A*, the total cost of each route only.
SELECT * FROM pgr_aStarCost('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost, x1, y1, x2, y2 FROM edges', [5, 3], [12, 17]);

presets.label: pgr_aStarCostMatrix
sql: -- A* costs between every ordered pair of the listed vertices.
SELECT * FROM pgr_aStarCostMatrix('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost, x1, y1, x2, y2 FROM edges', [5, 7, 12, 16]);

presets.label: pgr_bdAstar
sql: -- Bidirectional A*: from both ends at once.
SELECT * FROM pgr_bdAstar('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost, x1, y1, x2, y2 FROM edges', 5, 12);

presets.label: pgr_bdAstarCost
sql: -- Bidirectional A*, cost only.
SELECT * FROM pgr_bdAstarCost('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost, x1, y1, x2, y2 FROM edges', [5, 3], [12, 17]);

presets.label: pgr_bdAstarCostMatrix
sql: -- Bidirectional A* over every ordered pair.
SELECT * FROM pgr_bdAstarCostMatrix('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost, x1, y1, x2, y2 FROM edges', [5, 7, 12, 16]);

presets.label: pgr_bellmanFord
sql: -- Bellman-Ford also accepts negative costs (none in the sample data).
SELECT * FROM pgr_bellmanFord('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 5, [12, 17]);

presets.label: pgr_edwardMoore
sql: -- Edward Moore: a queue-based variant of Bellman-Ford.
SELECT * FROM pgr_edwardMoore('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 5, [12, 17]);

presets.label: pgr_dagShortestPath
sql: -- For a directed acyclic graph: the forward costs only (no reverse_cost).
SELECT * FROM pgr_dagShortestPath('SELECT id, source, target, cost FROM edges', 5, [11, 12]);

presets.label: pgr_binaryBreadthFirstSearch
sql: -- Costs must be 0 or 1: here even edge ids are free and odd ones cost 1.
SELECT * FROM pgr_binaryBreadthFirstSearch(
'SELECT id, source, target,
CASE WHEN id % 2 = 0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS cost,
CASE WHEN id % 2 = 0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS reverse_cost
FROM edges',

presets.label: pgr_johnson
sql: -- The cost between every pair of vertices that can reach each other (table only).
-- Johnson's algorithm suits sparse graphs.
SELECT * FROM pgr_johnson('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges');

presets.label: pgr_floydWarshall
sql: -- The same all-pairs costs by Floyd-Warshall, which suits dense graphs (table only).
SELECT * FROM pgr_floydWarshall('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges');

presets.label: pgr_ksp
sql: -- The three cheapest routes from 6 to 17 (Yen's algorithm), one colour per path_id.
SELECT * FROM pgr_ksp('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 6, 17, 3);

presets.label: pgr_trsp
sql: -- From 1 to 8 without the turns the restrictions table forbids (each path costs extra to take).
SELECT * FROM pgr_trsp('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT path, cost FROM restrictions', 1, 8);

presets.label: pgr_trsp_withPoints
sql: -- The same turn restrictions, from point 1 to vertex 10.

SELECT * FROM pgr_trsp_withPoints('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT path, cost FROM restrictions', 'SELECT pid, edge_id, fraction, side FROM pointsofinterest', -1, 10);

presets.label: pgr_trspVia
sql: -- A route through 5, 7, 1, 8 and 15 that obeys the turn restrictions.
SELECT * FROM pgr_trspVia('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT path, cost FROM restrictions', [5, 7, 1, 8, 15]);

presets.label: pgr_trspVia_withPoints
sql: -- Through point 6, vertex 15 and point 5, obeying the turn restrictions.

SELECT * FROM pgr_trspVia_withPoints('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT path, cost FROM restrictions', 'SELECT pid, edge_id, fraction, side FROM pointsofinterest', [-6, 15, -5]);

presets.label: pgr_turnRestrictedPath
sql: -- Up to three routes from 3 to 8 that take no restricted turn, ignoring edge direction;
-- on this graph only one exists.
SELECT * FROM pgr_turnRestrictedPath('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', 'SELECT path, cost FROM restrictions', 3, 8, 3, directed => false);

presets.label: pgr_TSP
sql: -- A round trip from 5 through 6, 10 and 15, from a matrix of shortest-path costs.
SELECT * FROM pgr_TSP(
$$SELECT * FROM pgr_dijkstraCostMatrix('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges', [5, 6, 10, 15], directed => false)$$,
start_id => 5);

presets.label: pgr_TSPeuclidean
sql: -- A round trip over every vertex by straight-line distance, from vertex 1.
SELECT * FROM pgr_TSPeuclidean('SELECT id, x, y FROM vertices', start_id => 1);

presets.label: pgr_connectedComponents
sql: -- Which vertices can reach each other, ignoring direction: the sample graph falls into three pieces,
-- each named after its smallest vertex.
SELECT * FROM pgr_connectedComponents('SELECT id, source, target, cost, reverse_cost FROM edges');

presets.label: pgr_extractVertices
sql: -- The vertex table rebuilt from the edges' source and target ids, with each vertex's edges.
SELECT * FROM pgr_extractVertices('SELECT id, source, target FROM edges');

presets.label: pgr_findCloseEdges (loads spatial)
sql: -- Geometry work needs duckdb-spatial; the first LOAD downloads it (about 24 MB).
LOAD spatial;
-- The two edges closest to a point within 0.5 units, with where the point projects onto each.
SELECT edge_id, fraction, side, distance, ST_AsText(geom) AS point, ST_AsText(edge) AS connector
FROM pgr_findCloseEdges('SELECT id, geom FROM edges', 'POINT(2.9 1.8)'::GEOMETRY, 0.5, cap => 2);

presets.label: pgr_version
sql: -- The pgRouting version built into the extension.
SELECT pgr_version();
